response.text:
Here’s a polished follow-up you can send to the vendor. I can schedule and send it Monday at 8:00 their time if you grant permission to send from your connected email account — otherwise I can only prepare the draft and give instructions for you to schedule it.

Draft email
Subject: Follow-up: delayed shipment for [Order/PO #]

Hello [Vendor Name],

I’m following up about the shipment for [Order/PO #], which was expected on [original delivery date]. We still haven’t received an update and this delay is impacting our schedule. Please confirm:

- Current status of the shipment
- Revised estimated delivery date
- Any issues or actions needed on our side to expedite

We appreciate a response by [date/time you want a response] so we can plan accordingly. If you’ve already shipped, please provide the tracking number and carrier.

Thank you,
[Your name]
[Your title / Company]
[Phone / email]

What I need from you to send/schedule this
1. Do you want me to send it on your behalf from a connected email account? If yes:
   - Confirm which account to send from (or connect the account/tool).
   - Provide the vendor’s email address.
   - Confirm the vendor’s timezone (or confirm “their time” means the vendor’s local time zone).
   - Confirm which Monday you mean (the next Monday is 2026-09-07) or give a specific date.
   - Any additions (order/PO #, original delivery date, response deadline, CCs, attachments).

2. If you do not want me to send it:
   - I can leave this draft ready and give step-by-step instructions to schedule it in Gmail/Outlook for Monday at 8:00 vendor time.

Note about scheduling and notifications
- I cannot continue working in the background or send the message later unless an email-sending/scheduling tool is available and you authorize its use. If you authorize sending now, I’ll schedule it for the specified time and confirm here once it’s been sent. Otherwise, tell me how you’d like to proceed.
